passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Overview Verizon Communications Inc. is a holding company that, acting through its subsidiaries, is one of the world’s leading providers of communications, technology, information and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses and government entities. With a presence around the world, we offer data, video and voice services and solutions on our networks and platforms that are designed to meet customers’ demand for mobility, reliable network connectivity and security. To compete effectively in today’s dynamic marketplace, we are focused on delivering what customers want and need in the digital world by offering innovative products and services, delivering excellent customer experience, and leveraging the capabilities of our high-performing networks. Highlights of Our 2025 Financial Results (dollars in millions) 21 Table of Contents Business Overview We have two reportable segments that we operate and manage as strategic business units - Consumer and Business. Revenue by Segment ——— Note: Excludes eliminations. Verizon Consumer Group Our Consumer segment provides consumer-focused wireless and wireline communications services and products. Our wireless services are provided across one of the most extensive wireless networks in the U.S. under the Verizon family of brands and through wholesale and other arrangements. As of the date this report is being filed, our wireline services are provided in 31 U.S. states and Washington D.C. over our 100% fiber-optic network through our fiber product portfolio, as well as over a traditional copper-based network. We also provide FWA broadband through our 5G or 4G LTE networks as an alternative to traditional landline internet access. Customers can obtain our wireless services on a postpaid or prepaid basis. Our postpaid service is generally billed one month in advance for a monthly access charge in return for access to and usage of network services. Our prepaid service is offered only to Consumer customers and enables individuals to obtain wireless services without credit verification by paying for all services in advance. The Consumer segment also offers several categories of wireless equipment to customers, including a variety of smartphones and other handsets, wireless-enabled internet devices, such as tablets, and other wireless-enabled connected devices, such as smart watches. In addition to wireless services and equipment for retail customers, the Consumer segment sells residential fixed connectivity solutions, including internet, video and voice services, and wireless network access to resellers on a wholesale basis. The Consumer segment's operating revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 totaled $106.8 billion, an increase of $3.9 billion, or 3.8%, compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. See "Segment Results of Operations" for additional information regarding our Consumer segment’s operating performance and selected operating statistics. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following discussion of "Risk Factors" identifies factors that may adversely affect our business, operations, financial condition or future performance. This information should be read in conjunction with "Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Result of Operations" and the consolidated financial statements and related notes. The following discussion of risks is not all-inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are the material factors to consider when evaluating our business and expectations. These factors could cause our future results to differ materially from our historical results and from expectations reflected in forward-looking statements. Economic and Strategic Risks We face significant competition that may negatively affect our operating results. We face significant competition in our industries. The rapid development of new technologies, services and products has eliminated many of the traditional distinctions among wireless, cable, internet and other communication services and brought new competitors to our markets, including other telecommunications companies, cable companies, wireless service providers, satellite providers, and others. While these changes have enabled us to offer new types of products and services, they have also allowed other providers to broaden the scope of their own competitive offerings. If we are unable to successfully differentiate our services and products from our competitors, it could adversely affect our competitive position and market share. Our competitors commonly offer aggressive pricing, promotions, premium content options and other incentives – in some cases specifically targeting our customers and putting pressure on our pricing and margins. In addition, we expect the wireless industry’s customer growth rate to continue to moderate over time in comparison to historical growth rates, leading to increased competition for customers. Our ability to compete effectively will depend on, among other things, the pricing of our products and services and our value proposition, our competitors' promotional strategies, the quality of our customer service, our network 11 Table of Contents reliability, speed, capacity and coverage, our ability to market our products and services effectively, our development of new and enhanced products and services, our capital resources, and the reach and quality of our sales and distribution channels. It will also depend on how successfully we anticipate and respond to various factors affecting our industries, including changes in consumer preferences and demand for existing services, new technologies and business models, such as the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies, demographic and immigration trends, evolving geopolitical and economic conditions, including inflation, and regulatory changes. If we are not able to respond successfully to these competitive challenges, our results of operations and financial condition could be adversely impacted. credit_strengths.text: Verizon's revenue base is large and growing, with the top line expanding across the annual trend series while operating income also improved, supporting a stable earnings profile. Operating margin sits above the sector median, indicating better cost absorption than peers. This scale and margin position underpin the issuer's ability to generate recurring cash flow from its wireless and wireline subscriber base.

Operating cash flow remains substantial and has been broadly stable across the trend period, comfortably covering reported interest expense. Interest coverage is near the sector median, and the cash balance provides a meaningful liquidity buffer. This cash generation supports the issuer's ability to service debt through the cycle despite a capital-intensive network.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows a large concentration of maturities beyond the fifth year, but the next twelve months still carry a sizeable repayment burden. The issuer also relies on asset-backed debt and floating-rate obligations, which exposes it to refinancing and rate risk. This maturity profile requires continued capital markets access.

The risk factors highlight intense competition and moderating wireless customer growth, with rivals offering aggressive pricing and promotions that pressure margins. A sustained revenue or earnings decline could impair the reporting unit and affect financial condition. This is a concrete competitive threat to the issuer's cash-flow durability.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Net leverage sits modestly above the sector median and just below the next threshold, leaving limited headroom. A small EBITDA decline or debt increase could push leverage into a weaker tier. Interest coverage is adequate but below the sector median, so debt service capacity is sensitive to earnings volatility.

Operating cash flow covers reported interest expense multiple times, but the absence of capex data prevents a full free-cash-flow assessment. Dividends absorb a large share of operating cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity. The current ratio is below one and below the sector median, indicating tight near-term liquidity.

overall_credit_view.text: Verizon's credit profile is supported by scale, stable operating cash flow and a diversified funding base, but leverage is above the sector median and cash-flow coverage is weaker than peers. The indicative financial risk profile is significant, with leverage near a tier boundary. We view the outlook as stable but sensitive to competitive pressure and refinancing conditions.

The debt maturity ladder is long-dated, yet near-term repayments and asset-backed borrowings require ongoing market access. Shareholder distributions consume most operating cash flow, constraining deleveraging. Missing capex data limits free-cash-flow analysis, which is material to assessing true debt-servicing capacity. We would monitor leverage headroom and competitive trends closely.

credit_strengths.text: Verizon的收入基礎龐大且持續增長，年度趨勢系列中頂線擴張，同時營運收入亦有所改善，支撐穩定的盈利狀況。營運利潤率處於行業中位數之上，顯示成本吸收能力優於同業。此規模及利潤率定位鞏固發行人從其無線及有線用戶基礎產生經常性現金流的能力。
營運現金流仍然可觀，並在趨勢期間大致穩定，足以舒適地覆蓋報告利息支出。利息覆蓋率接近行業中位數，而現金結餘提供有意義的流動性緩衝。此現金產生支撐發行人在資本密集型網絡下於週期內償付債務的能力。

key_risks.text: 債務票據顯示大量到期債務集中於第五年之後，但未來十二個月仍背負可觀的還款負擔。發行人亦依賴資產支持債務及浮動利率債務，使其面臨再融資及利率風險。此到期結構需要持續進入資本市場。
風險因素凸顯激烈競爭及無線客戶增長放緩，競爭對手提供進取定價及推廣，對利潤率構成壓力。收入或盈利持續下滑可能減值報告單位並影響財務狀況。這是對發行人現金流持久性的具體競爭威脅。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 淨槓桿略高於行業中位數，並僅低於下一門檻，留下有限空間。EBITDA小幅下降或債務增加可能將槓桿推入較弱級別。利息覆蓋率充足但低於行業中位數，因此債務償付能力對盈利波動敏感。
營運現金流覆蓋報告利息支出數倍，但缺乏資本開支數據阻礙全面自由現金流評估。股息吸收營運現金流的一大部分，限制去槓桿能力。流動比率低於一且低於行業中位數，顯示近期流動性緊張。

overall_credit_view.text: Verizon的信用狀況受規模、穩定營運現金流及多元化資金基礎支撐，但槓桿高於行業中位數，且現金流覆蓋弱於同業。指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，槓桿接近級別邊界。我們認為展望穩定，但對競爭壓力及再融資條件敏感。
債務到期階梯屬長期，但近期還款及資產支持借款需要持續市場准入。股東分派消耗大部分營運現金流，限制去槓桿。缺失資本開支數據限制自由現金流分析，而該分析對評估真實債務償付能力至關重要。我們將密切監察槓桿空間及競爭趨勢。
